channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal tightrope shapes outlook – OCBC
item.description: OCBC strategists Sim Moh Siong and Christopher Wong highlight that hopes of a fiscally conservative Chancellor under incoming United Kingdom (UK) Prime Minister Burnham have supported the British Pound (GBP) and gilts.

item.title: British Pound eases against Yen after hitting highest level since 2007
item.description: GBP/JPY trades with a mild negative bias on Thursday, taking a breather after climbing to its highest level since December 2007 the previous day, as the British Pound benefited from easing political uncertainty and expectations of greater fiscal discipline.

item.title: US Initial Jobless Claims dropped to 208K last week
item.description: According to a report from the US Department of Labor (DOL) released on Thursday, the number of US citizens submitting new applications for unemployment insurance shrank to 208K for the week ending July 11.

item.title: United States Retail Sales rise 0.2% in June to $768.6 billion
item.description: Retail Sales in the United States (US) rose by 0.2% on a monthly basis in June to $768.6 billion, the US Census Bureau reported on Thursday. This print followed the 1% increase recorded in May and came in line with the market expectation. On a yearly basis, Retail Sales were up 6.7%.

item.title: US Dollar Index: Decline seen overdone – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad notes the US Dollar (USD) has steadied near a one‑month low after softer United States (US) Producer Price Index (PPI) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) data weighed on Fed funds pricing.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC hold and guidance shift – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities notes the Bank of Canada (BoC) kept its policy rate at 2.25% and softened guidance by removing references to both rate-cut risks and consecutive hikes. Markets interpreted the statement as mildly dovish, but prior moves limited volatility.

item.title: European Central Bank: Hawkish hold bias – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Bas van Geffen expects the ECB to keep the deposit rate at 2.25% in July, judging a hike as a tail risk that would require a much stronger energy shock.

item.title: Euro: Policy divergence and carry flows – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu says iFlow Carry is beginning to resemble its 2023 upswing. Neutral positioning in carry currencies, including those funded in the dollar, leaves room for exposures to rebuild. G10 FX attracted broad inflows, while EM FX selling was led by HUF, ZAR and KRW.

item.title: Silver tumbles as energy-driven inflation fears keep rate outlook elevated
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) falls toward $56.70 at the time of writing on Thursday, down 1.85% on the day. The white metal comes under selling pressure as renewed tensions between the United States (US) and Iran drive energy prices higher, reviving concerns about persistently elevated global inflation.

item.title: British Pound: Shorts on the run – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner highlights a powerful short squeeze in Sterling, triggered by reports that Shabana Mahmood could become Andy Burnham’s chancellor, a choice seen as less fiscally expansive.

item.title: Gold slips as energy-driven inflation fears keep Fed rate hike bets in play
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) edges lower on Thursday as traders look past back-to-back softer-than-expected US inflation reports and remain focused on renewed Middle East tensions, which are fueling concerns that higher energy prices could reignite inflationary pressure.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: BoC on hold and hikes priced out – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s (BBH) Elias Haddad reports USD/CAD is consolidating losses after benign United States (US) Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Producer Price Index (PPI) data, with the Bank of Canada (BoC) leaving its policy rate unchanged at 2.25% for a sixth meeting.

item.title: Euro turns upside down as US Dollar bounces back
item.description: The Euro (EUR) trades marginally lower to near 1.1460 against the US Dollar (USD) during the European trading session on Thursday after giving back its early gains.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Mixed range trade outlook against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that USD/JPY has seen a slight increase in downward momentum, pointing to a lower intraday range around 161.70–162.30.

item.title: US Dollar: Retail sales slowdown view – TD Securities
item.description: TD Securities’ macro team expects June US Retail Sales to stagnate at 0.0% month-on-month, versus the consensus 0.2%. They see weakness led by the control group, negative gasoline sales from falling prices, and a drop in food services, partly offset by strong auto sales.

item.title: Indian Rupee falls further amid higher oil prices, FIIs extend selling streak
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) trades lower against the US Dollar (USD), extending its losing streak for the third trading day on Thursday. The USD/INR pair rises to near 96.32 as elevated crude oil prices have renewed fears of higher foreign outflows.

item.title: Gold Price Forecast: XAU/USD stays below 20-day EMA, sees further downside below $3,940
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) is down 0.7% to near $4,030 during the European trading session on Thursday. The precious metal faces selling pressures as global inflation concerns remain intact amid elevated energy prices in the wake of widening military aggression between the United States (US) and Iran.

item.title: British Pound rallies to multi-month highs on reports of Mahmood appointment
item.description: The British Pound (GBP) has staged a broad-based rally across major currency pairs, hitting multi-month highs against both the US Dollar (USD) and the Euro (EUR).

item.title: Brazilian Real: Below 50dma opens move to 5.00 – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale highlights that USD/BRL has retreated to 5.07 after threatening 5.20 earlier in July, with the Brazilian Real (BRL) retaining a firm tone following soft United States (US) Producer Price Index (PPI) and lower Treasury yields.

item.title: Euro rises vs British Pound amid hawkish ECB comments, mixed UK economic data
item.description: EUR/GBP trades around 0.8485 on Thursday, up 0.24% at the time of writing, as investors digest a mixed batch of UK economic data and continued hawkish comments from European Central Bank (ECB) policymakers.

item.title: Australian Dollar consolidates gains as dwindling Fed hiking hopes hurt the US Dollar
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) trades practically flat against a weaker US Dollar (USD) on Thursday as investors pare back bets of immediate Fed tightening, following unexpectedly soft US inflation figures earlier in the week.

item.title: Crude oil loading suspended at all Iraqi terminals after drone incident – Reuters
item.description: Citing four Iraqi oil and security sources, Reuters reported on Thursday that a drone crashed into an oil tanker in Iraq's Basra terminal, although no damage or fire was caused.

item.title: British Pound: Fiscal reassurance supports gains – MUFG
item.description: Lee Hardman at MUFG highlights that the British Pound (GBP) has strengthened sharply, helped by reports that Shabana Mahmood is set to become the next UK chancellor, reinforcing expectations of “sound public finances” under Prime Minister in-waiting Andy Burnham.

item.title: US Dollar: Losing more ground – ING
item.description: ING strategists Francesco Pesole, Frantisek Taborsky and Chris Turner note the Dollar remains under pressure after softer US CPI and PPI data, with FX volatility declining and Brent around $85.

item.title: Silver price today: Silver falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Silver prices (XAG/USD) fell on Thursday, according to FXStreet data. Silver trades at $57.00 per troy ounce, down 1.34% from the $57.77 it cost on Wednesday.

item.title: Euro remains stronger against Canadian Dollar following Eurozone Trade Balance data
item.description: EUR/CAD extends its gains for the second successive day, trading around 1.6100 during the European hours on Thursday.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar: Kiwi vulnerable to softer data – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur notes that the New Zealand Dollar has recovered about 2 cents since the latest rate hike, with markets now effectively pricing in nearly one additional hike by year-end.

item.title: GBP/USD Price Forecast: Dip-buying favored on pullbacks below 1.3500
item.description: The GBP/USD pair attracts some sellers on Thursday and erodes a part of the previous day's strong gains to an over two-month high, around the 1.3555-1.3560 region.

item.title: WTI remains broadly firm near $79 amid continued US-Iran aggression
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI), futures on NYMEX, trade 0.9% lower to near $79.00 during the European trading session on Thursday, but is closer to its monthly high of $80.61 posted on Tuesday.

item.title: Australian Dollar: Momentum points to higher levels against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: United Overseas Bank’s (UOB) Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note that AUD/USD has broken above significant resistance at 0.7015, with price action extending to 0.7021. In the next 24 hours, the Australian Dollar is expected to stay in a higher 0.6985–0.7025 range.
